patient_information: A 71-year-old Japanese man, born and living in Kyushu district, southern Japan.
chief_complaint: Nodular lesion in his right lung requiring work-up.
history_of_present_illness: A lung lesion detected 2 years prior as linear, evolved into a 2 cm nodular lesion in the right lung.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Born and living in Kyushu district, southern Japan, with no history of travelling overseas.
physical_exam: Clear chest and normal remainder of physical examination.
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count (WBC 6.5 x 10^9/L, Eosinophils 8.3%, Total eosinophil count 0.54 x 10^9/L), elevated IgE (185.7 U/mL), normal liver and renal function tests, normal electrolytes, not raised LDH and CRP. Serologies for Cryptococcus Ag, Aspergillus Ag, β-D-glucan (6.0 pg/mL), and QuantiFERON test were negative. Imaging included chest radiography and CT scan revealing a nodular lesion, and FDG-PET-CT showing increased FDG-uptake in the right upper lobe lesion. Bronchoscopy and BAL fluid cytology were negative for malignant cells and acid-fast bacilli, and a wide range of tumor markers were negative. Multiple-dot ELISA was strongly positive for P. westermani.
differential_diagnosis: Pulmonary tuberculosis, lung cancer, inflammatory lesions, infectious processes (excluding endemic mycoses due to geography), and pulmonary helminth infections, especially paragonimiasis.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was treated with oral praziquantel 25 mg/kg tds for 3 consecutive days, resulting in the lung lesion gradually fading and disappearing, and a decline in serum antibody titre.

Histopathology of the nodular lung lesion that was surgically resected after diagnosis of lung cancer based on FDG-PET imaging. Note the chronic granulomatous lesion containing numerous Paragonimus eggs (black arrows). Foreign body giant cells (white arrows) are also seen in the tissue.
